proposals.evidence: DEDR 3986(a) documents the pal tooth family: Kodagu pallï, Malayalam pallu, Tamil pal, Malto palu, Kolami pal, Gadaba pal/pallū with plural palkīl, and Toda pas̱. Survey plural and final-vowel material (including palku, pālkill, pāldu) remains unchanged. Toda parse is a comparative correspondence to its distinctive s̱ reflex; Betta Kurumba pallə extends the comparison to a lect absent from this article. Subsection (b) toothstick compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 474 explicitly documents Kannada eraḍu, Kodagu daṇḍï, Kota eyḏ, Kurukh irb (two persons), Kuwi rindi, Malayalam raṇṭu, Parji adjectival ir, Tamil reṇṭu and Toda ēḍ. The survey cognacy annotations independently identify the article. Final vowels and the Kurukh personal versus Parji adjectival use are retained; no grammatical category is silently added to the generic survey gloss two. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 1931 explicitly marks Kodagu cōpï red/redness and its associated cō- forms as borrowed from Malayalam. The same article gives Malayalam cōppu red/red colour/ruby. Survey Kodagu cōpə is therefore proposed as borrowed from the existing Malayalam cōppu attestation, preserving its final-vowel transcription and immediate donor.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 1514 directly gives Kodagu tittï, Kolami kis, Malto cicu and Toda tït fire. Badaga kiccə is supported indirectly by the article’s explicit identification of Toda kic as a Badaga loan; this proposal is for the Badaga source form, not for the borrowed Toda song word. Survey titta, kiss, cicadu and tīttə preserve their endings and transcriptions. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4449 gives Kodagu pēnï, Tamil pēṉ, Kolami pēn and Kannada pēn louse. Survey final vowels are retained. Kannada hēnu is a comparative modern p-to-h correspondence, explicitly questioned rather than literally listed by the source; Kolami pānu retains its vowel difference for review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
